description:
Move a broadcast to the trash: its public link and stream addresses stop working for listeners.
Use: a broadcast that will not run again. For 30 days update_broadcast with restore true brings it back with the same link (list_broadcasts with lifecycle archived lists the trash); after that the broadcast is erased for good. Ending a live run: update_broadcast with onAir false.
Arguments: broadcastId only, from list_broadcasts or start_broadcast, upper or lower case. A transcriptionId is not_found (delete_transcription removes a recording); the short code in the link is invalid_options. Example: {broadcastId: "0190f0e0-7c1a-7d3e-9b2a-5f4e3d2c1b0a"}.
Behaviour: free, and a soft delete: nothing is erased for 30 days, and one already in the trash is left as it is, so a retry is safe. At once every connected listener is signed out. A broadcast on air is refused: end its run first (update_broadcast with onAir false). The transcriptions it recorded are not deleted: while it is in the trash they leave list_transcriptions and search_transcriptions, get_transcription still reads them by id, and delete_transcription deletes one. Restoring (update_broadcast with restore true) brings back the same link and broadcastId, its settings and its transcriptions; listeners get back in by opening the link again (with the same listener code when private). Gives rate_limited (with retryAfterS) past 600 calls a minute per API key.
Returns: broadcastId, name, deleted true, deletedAt, restorableUntil.
Errors: invalid_state while on air; not_found for an unknown broadcastId; invalid_options for something that is not a UUID; forbidden for a read-only key.

broadcastId.description: A broadcastId from list_broadcasts or start_broadcast, of a broadcast that is not on air.

name: delete_broadcast
title: Delete a broadcast
